correctness.rationale: Deleting a cycle edge leaves a spanning tree, whose incidence roots are an integer basis of A_(n−1), of covolume √n. The sole cycle dependence has coefficient sum δ; when nonzero, subtracting the deleted vertex from the remaining tree roots gives a rank-one determinant update with absolute determinant |δ|, giving the full-dimensional simplex formula. When balanced, the cycle integrability condition defines h uniquely modulo constants, the unique dependence is affine, and every root belongs to the same height-one hyperplane in the root space. In its circuit subdivision, shift convex coefficients in the negative direction of the cycle relation until a positive-support coefficient vanishes. This endpoint is unique, and lying in two deletion simplices requires a zero at both corresponding indices, so interiors are disjoint. There are ℓ/2 deletion simplices. Each is the height-one base of a spanning-tree pyramid of volume √n/(n−1)! and height 1/∥h−h̄1∥, yielding the stated Euclidean volume. In the leaf family the attachment is the height-zero vertex of the listed (0,1,2,1) cycle (the convention used in the proof). The energy n(t+6)−(4+2a−t)² attains its minimum 2n uniquely at a=t and maximum at the nearest permitted 4+2a−t to zero, with the stated parity and small t exceptions. Bridge-root sign changes give a lattice automorphism in a tree basis that fixes the omitted cycle root. Each deletion simplex is unimodular in the height-one lattice because the tree basis elements all have height one and their differences span the integral height-zero kernel. Thus the common normalized volume is 2. The independent exact Gram calculation checks actual coordinates, including nδ² in a nonbalanced case and both deletion simplices across 63 small leaf patterns; it does not prove the all-graph formulas.
residual_risks: The sharp family statement uses attachment at the minimum of the oriented cycle height. Attachment at a middle height is a different family. The ratio is unbounded as the fixed-graph comparison is repeated for larger t, not on one finite graph; the two dimension cases are not directly comparable.
